Jake Roberts DDTs Booker T for the pin. Stevie Ray runs in to protect Sharmell but is clotheslined and beaten back before the finish.
Gary Hart's J-Tex Corporation upsets the Steiner Brothers — Muta's kick to the throat sets up Chono's pin on Rick Steiner, who is stretchered out gasping for air.

Lance Storm wins his first XWF Cruiserweight Championship on a small package after Dynamite Kid's flying head butt misses; Dynamite mauls Storm with the belt afterward. (XWF Cruiserweight Championship)
Big Bossman beats North American Champion Vader's manager Harley Race with an Alabama Slam; Vader attacks Bossman with a Power Bomb afterward.

Samoa Joe wins by disqualification (not the title) after manager Harley Race blindsides him with a diving head butt off the top rope while Joe has Vader locked in the Coquina Clutch; the Big Bossman runs in afterward for a post-match brawl. (XWF North American Heavyweight Championship)

Francine, torn between her two clients, slaps Douglas and is shoved down for it; the distraction lets Rude hit the Rude Awakening. Rude and Francine leave together.

matches.note: Billed as a 30-man Rumble; the served play-by-play individually names only 29 entrants — a gap in the fed's own text, registered rather than guessed at. Jim Cornette corners Owen Hart; Colonel Robert Parker corners Windham/Blanchard; Chyna corners Sabu, the only entrant from Matthew Hopkins' own Corporate Dynasty.

Wight retains — ICWC GM Eric Bischoff runs in with a bag of thumb tacks; Cactus Jack fights him off with the Mandible Claw, but Wight recovers to choke slam Cactus onto the tacks for the pin. (XWF World Heavyweight Championship)
DiBiase's henchmen Virgil and IRS drag him out the cage door for a technical escape victory just as Orndorff piledrives him.
Power & Glory win — Hercules Hernandez traps Scott Taylor in the Full Nelson for the submission.
Rude wins with the Fisherman's Suplex on the steel ramp; Miss Brooks corners Rude.

Yokozuna wins by hip toss, guest-announced by Michael Buffer, Mr. Fuji managing. Afterward Demolition — furious at being cost the XWF Tag Titles by Fuji's own Yokozuna — shockingly aligns with Fuji and Yokozuna, declaring their sights on ICWC's own tag scene.
DDP wins by countout; Bigelow attacks him and Kimberly Page afterward, and Page fires back with the Diamond Cutter.

Champion Sherri Martel retains via a small package the referee doesn't see clean — guest cornerwoman Trish Stratus kicks Moolah first, then turns on the crowd, and Sherri belts her afterward for it. (UWF World Women's Championship)
Champion James Storm retains, cracking a beer bottle into Piper's face and rolling him up; Miss Jacqueline Moore is in Storm's corner. (UWF United States Championship)
Billed as the UWF World Tag Team Champions (Animal & Hawk) against Team 3D, but never for the title — the match degenerates into a full ringside brawl and the referee rules a double disqualification.
Dustin Rhodes grabs the glove and pins Sting clean after injuring his leg early. Dusty Rhodes looks on from afar.
Lesnar's valet Rena Mero distracts Angle out of the Ankle Lock, letting Lesnar hit the F5 for the pin; Hopkins fires Angle from the UWF afterward.
The Owner sends Chyna to the back before the bell, wrestles Christian Cage competitively, and still loses to the Unprettier.
Andre's team wins in near-record time — Mae Young's top-rope splash finishes Heenan after Andre slams King Kong Bundy.

Main event. Champion Flair retains — a fireball to the face, brass knuckles, and a spinebuster off the top rope through a flaming table, capped by a fire-extinguisher-assisted pin. Woman and Arn Anderson corner Flair; Matthew Hopkins and Chyna corner Abyss; Howard Finkel is the special guest ring announcer. (UWF World Heavyweight Championship)

name: UWOW Brand New Fear (Jan '09)
notes: Relocated from a uwf-uwow placeholder row of the same nominal date: the served card's own text bills this explicitly as a joint UWOW-banner presentation across UWF, ICWC and XWF, not a UWF-only show.

matches.note: The Firm (Rhodes & DiBiase, managed by the Million Dollar Man Ted DiBiase) beat XWF World Tag Team Champions Harlem Heat — DiBiase's Dream Street on Stevie Ray, then Rhodes' Bionic Elbow to finish Booker T. Not a title match; the Million Dollar Man grabs both the UWF and XWF Tag belts afterward but only gets to keep the UWF ones, since neither was actually on the line.
Savage, still mocking the Ultimate Warrior's mannerisms after their falling-out, catches a dazed Jarrett with a double axehandle for the pin.
Champion Noble retains — Race misses a diving head butt off the top rope, and Noble rolls him up. Race lays Noble out with the belt afterward. (UWF United States Championship)

The Bossman becomes champion after Rude's own ringside allies (Great Khali, Magnus Hassan, Sheik Daivari, led out by Sheik Adnan el Kaisse) turn the match into a numbers game; a wayward elbow from Rude bumps the referee, and when Khali's chop misses the Bossman and clips Rude instead, the Bossman covers for the pin. (International Heavyweight Championship — billed inconsistently across the fed's own text as both ICWC's and XWF's own belt in the same segment; the discrepancy is recorded rather than silently resolved)

Doink wins with a reversed kiss and a headbutt-into-small-package; Brother Love, Bastien Booger and Damien Demento corner Doink and brawl with McMahon loyalists Pat Patterson and Gerald Brisco at ringside.
Champion Natalya retains — Victoria's leg-pull denies Madusa's own Back Draft cover, and Natalya reverses into a back suplex/power bomb pin. (XWF X-Treme Divas Championship)

A three-on-one ambush, not a contest: Shawn Michaels superkicks the Undertaker, Triple H and Ric Flair join in, a second superkick follows, and Mr. Perfect finishes with a steel chair to draw the first blood.
Kennedy hits the Mic Check on Hart for the pin after Sting and Jim Neidhart's ringside argument leaves Hart exposed; Hart & Sting's team is eliminated from the Battle Bowl process.
Randy Savage and Miss Elizabeth's ringside arrival distracts the Warrior long enough for Abyss to spear him and pin; Abyss & Animal advance. Chyna corners Abyss.
Batista Bombs Mark Henry for the pin; the Rock & Batista advance.
Randy Orton's ringside arrival lures Andre away from the corner, leaving Hawk exposed to Cage's Unprettier; Jericho & Cage advance.
Hogan gets the hot tag and finishes CM Punk with the big boot and leg drop; Hogan & Hardy advance.

matches.note: Champion Angle sets up a Con-Chair-To on Edge with Edge's own chair, but Sid boots Jarrett out of harm's way and Double Choke Slams Angle & Edge instead; Sid then Power Bombs Jarrett, but Edge spears Sid for the pin — Edge leaves as the new ICWC World Heavyweight Champion, also still holding the Intercontinental belt. Angle walks out on his own title match without explanation. (ICWC World Heavyweight Championship)

The Radicalz retain — Jim Cornette's own tennis racquet backfires when Malenko takes it from him to blast Davey Boy Smith, and Malenko finishes Owen Hart with the Texas Cloverleaf. (ICWC World Tag Team Championship)

A shocking swerve: after Lesnar hits the F-U... err, after Cena hits the FU on Lesnar and covers, his own partner Big Show breaks it up with a leg drop, then choke slams Cena and rolls Lesnar on top for the pin.
Vader wins with a big splash, then Power Bombs Orndorff repeatedly afterward, stretchering him out.
Umaga finishes Matt Hardy with the Samoan Spike.

Randy Orton becomes the new UWF World Heavyweight Champion, RKO'ing a stunned JBL after JBL's own manager Ted DiBiase's interference backfires; Mr. Perfect's ringside chair shot on Flair earlier had already thinned the field. Fills the vacancy the served uwf-uwow corpus's own Starrcade 2008 crawl left open (see that wing's own tier-3 gap note). (UWF World Heavyweight Championship (vacant, tournament final))

Billed as Hopkins accepting Triple H's open challenge, but the match is really a squash-then-angle: Triple H Pedigrees Hopkins repeatedly before the bout is swallowed by the Stephanie McMahon kidnapping angle (a second masked man clubs Triple H, and Jeff Jarrett, Kurt Angle and Sting are revealed working for Hopkins/TNA) — no finish is ever called. Vince McMahon, Shane McMahon, Stephanie McMahon and Shawn Michaels are all ringside for the McMahon side; Scott Hall and Kevin Nash flank Hopkins. (WWE World Heavyweight Championship — open challenge)
